posts.excerpt: A slow itinerary through neighborhood markets and railway towns, with a few notes on getting there.
posts.content:
# A Field Guide to Southeast Asia

A slow itinerary through neighborhood markets and railway towns, with a few notes on getting there.

## Arrive before the rush

Early trains bring the best conversations. Leave the morning open, walk the platform, and ask a stallholder what people order for breakfast. Write the route down while the details are fresh.

# Building Scalable Microservices

Trace a request across a small system and discover which contracts, timeouts, and tests make it dependable.

## Follow one request

Draw the call chain for one customer action. Record the owner and timeout at each boundary. A request ID shared by the services makes it possible to reconstruct the story after an incident.

# Getting Started with React Hooks

Hooks connect component state to the events that change it. A small example makes the dependency array and cleanup behavior easier to inspect.

## A sensor on the screen

Start with one input, such as a value typed into a search box. Store it in state and log the render where it changes. Add an effect only when a value must stay synchronized with something outside React.

Build a morning routine that fits the life you have, starting with one repeatable habit.

## Make tomorrow easier

Put the kettle, cup, and notebook together before going to bed. By removing one decision in advance you make it easier to begin a routine when attention is scarce.

## Finish in the pan

Lift the pasta a minute early and let its last minute happen in the sauce. A splash of cloudy cooking water loosens the pan while helping oil and starch come together.

Discover how solo travel builds confidence through small decisions, unfamiliar streets, and unexpected conversations.

## Keep a simple rhythm

Choose one place to explore each morning and keep the afternoon loose. A notebook, a modest budget, and the name of the nearest station are often enough to find your way home.
